steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Hello, Lara.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: 'The Spire hid amongst the mist, and the rain dripped onto the thousands of umbrellas...'

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Oh, hello, Doctor.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Sorry to disturb you while you're reading. How are you feeling?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Uhh, my wounds don't hurt so much anymore, but I still get dizzy pretty often and can't see things clearly.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Have you had any problems with the IV drip? Is it comfortable? Does anything feel off?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: My arm feels kinda cold, but I got used to it.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Doctor, how many more days will I have to stay on IV?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Hm... That depends.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Will it be much longer? I wanna go out for a walk.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I've been in bed for days. Even though I haven't moved an inch, it really tires me out.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: It won't be much longer, but your wounds are still healing. We'll let you walk around once they're better.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: That said...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The bloodwork is back for the girl who was caught in the Originium bomb blast. Her condition is clearly worsening.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: We managed to slow down the deterioration somewhat, but... *sigh*. It's an acute infection, and she had all these open wounds. We've done all the emergency treatment we could.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Based on the imaging tests, the Originium in her body is starting to put pressure on her optic nerves.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yes, she noticed something was off herself. Her vision blurs sometimes.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Even with suppressants, we haven't yet managed to stabilize her condition. At this rate, she's likely to go blind.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: How would she react if I told her, though? Would she be able to bear it?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: If I were the one on the bed, maybe I'd think it's better to know the truth, no matter how harsh it is.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: But she doesn't know fear yet. Her long nightmare has yet to begin. If I can let her have peace of mind, even for only a few more days...

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Okay, I get it. Even after I can move, the doctors will still need to observe my condition a little longer. I'll only be discharged from Rhodes Island when my Oripathy is stabilized.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: But yesterday, another doctor told me that Rhodes Island's a big ship, and I'm allowed to leave the hospital wing and visit other places as long as I take someone from medical with me.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: She even brought me a book from the library.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Right, Rhodes Island's a big place. There's a lot you can do here.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: For now though, I need to redress your wounds. Don't worry about what I'm doing and keep reading.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Is it okay if I read out loud? I don't want to hear the tweezers and medicine bottles.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yes, of course.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: 'Having forgotten my umbrella, I saw someone standing underneath the roof of a cafe on the other side of the street... A strange woman.'

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: 'The way she is dressed is very... not with the times. With a harp in her hand, she quietly... starts singing to the rain.'

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: 'The musical notes waft toward me continuously. After a while, I finally make out the words she is singing...'

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: The words... she is singing... uhh...

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: 'Please forget about me, just like the early spring snow.'

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Sorry, I couldn't help myself.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Oh, don't be sorry.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: You should close your eyes and get some rest. Maybe you've been reading too much. Your eyes are tired, and that's why you couldn't make out the letters.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Doctor, have you read this book before?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yes, but the movie adaptation is more famous. I've seen it several times, and I couldn't help but finish the quote when I heard it.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: What does the protagonist look like in the movie? I think of her as kind of tall with red hair, and she does this face when she talks—

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: —Wwrr!

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: D-Don't move now. The wounds on your face aren't too deep, but they still need time to heal.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: I don't think the actress they cast for the movie is quite like what you had in mind.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: That said, the movie and the book are completely different stories to begin with.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: If I were you, I would finish the book first and let my imagination flourish before seeing how the movie adapted things.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Okay, I won't ask for any more spoilers then. Once I'm done with the book, I'll watch the movie myself.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Oh, but I'm Infected now... They don't let Infected into movie theaters, do they?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I used to go to the movies with Mommy. The two of us always bought a huge tub of popcorn.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: She told me to never talk during a movie. I know you have to wait till it's over before you ask about the things you didn't get.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: So I'm a good girl, right...?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Don't cry. At the very least, you can watch movies in the AV room here on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: The screens aren't as big as the ones at the theaters, but it might be the perfect size for watching a movie alone, or with a few friends.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Even if it's just immersing yourself in the movie's sounds.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: In that case, take me to see it as soon as I can get out of bed.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Eh? Me? But I...

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: You're thinking of leaving Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Right. I've been here for quite a while now. Before I knew it, I'd already gotten to know everyone here so well.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: ...To the point that it's starting to scare me.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: N-Not that I'm afraid of you.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Yeah, I know.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Have you figured out when you're leaving?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: I got a new patient recently. I want to wait until her condition is more stable.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Should I keep it a secret, then?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yes, please. I don't want to tell anyone something so... depressing.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Sorry, but I'll probably be very busy, and I can't make any promises.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: No worries. I'll ask the other doctors, then.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: There, we're done. Does it feel off anywhere?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: No, not at all. Thanks.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Oh, wait up. Could you help me adjust the bookstand? I can't make out the words very well.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I think the Oripathy might've made me near-sighted.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: No, this isn't nearsightedness.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: But it's true that it will affect your vision. As for how much... we can't tell for sure yet.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: You should keep reading your books, but be sure to take a look at the beautiful scenery outside the window too.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: So the girl is going blind, but you haven't told her? And she wants to watch a movie?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Right. I couldn't bring myself to commit to anything. Telling her either the truth or a lie would be too cruel.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: But you want to make her wish come true, right?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: If I could, I'd love to watch a movie with her.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: It'd be even better if there were a ticket stub to keep. After all, it will be my last movie here on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: It's just... she might not get to see it.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: In terms of both venue and technical requirements, it's not all that hard to put together one of the relatively formal movie screenings we've held on Rhodes Island before.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: So you think I should've said yes to her?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Obviously that's for you to decide, as her doctor.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: All I'm saying is that, even if it's just for yourself, you could hold a movie screening and keep the ticket stub to commemorate your departure.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Just for myself...

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: But I'm afraid I don't know who to ask to set up a temporary movie theater.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Don't worry, I can help with that. It's not in my department's usual wheelhouse, but nothing a little engineering can't solve.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: And if requiring tickets is that important to you... Right, maybe we could add an automatic ticketing machine. That way, you won't need anyone to staff it, which will probably make things easier on you.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Don't mention it. This is nothing.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: I just hope it'll leave you with some pleasant memories.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Hello, Doctor.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Are you... the doctor who talks to me about movies?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Sorry, I can't see very well, so I can only try to guess by your footsteps. Sorry if I got it wrong.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: No, you got it right. Hello, Lara.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Oh, that's wonderful.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: What should I call you? Most of the doctors here have badges, but you don't.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Oh, don't worry about my name.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: It's time to give you another checkup.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Mm. Okay.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Doctor, I'm actually a little scared.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: My eyesight is getting worse and worse, but nobody will tell me what's going on.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I know there's no cure to Oripathy, but... I'm not ready... Am I about to...?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: You're overthinking it. Your life isn't in danger, for the time being.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Your Oripathy has been gradually stabilizing, and the wounds on your legs and abdomen have healed up very well.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Once we have the results of this checkup, we'll know for sure when we can take out the stitches.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Soon, maybe in a couple of days, we can let you watch a movie.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Oh, right.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: It also just so happens that Rhodes Island will hold a movie screening soon, and it's the one that's based on the book you're reading.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Let's go see it together, once you're out of bed.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Yay! It's a promise!

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yep, it's a promise.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Then... will you keep telling me the story during the checkup?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I want to read it myself, but it really tires me out to read now.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Close your eyes and get some rest.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: If I remember correctly, last time we got to the part where the protagonist and the wandering bard from the past reached a Leithanian nomadic city.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: She had never gone inside a nomadic city. She was terrified just from having to take the elevator at the entrance.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: The city must be a noisy place to a bard.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yes, very. She relied on her sensitive ears to tell pitches apart, but everything was so loud in the city.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: She'd never seen instruments with Arts Units that were tuned by machines. The music they played was like a kind of Originium Art in itself. She was completely mesmerized.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Moreover, the city was very affectionate to her. Many of the Spires' masters invited her as their guest.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: But she's from the past. She has to figure out a way to go back.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Hmm... Actually, there isn't anywhere she can go back to.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: —Oh, maybe we should make this a cliffhanger! I'll find out the ending for myself when we watch the movie.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: ...Right, Lara.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: When we watch the movie, aside from what's on the screen, there will be lots of sounds, too.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Like the bard strumming her instrument and singing, the chirping of the fowlbeasts, the winds blowing through the vast forest as they travel, and the rain that falls on the forest hut's roof.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: And since we'll be watching the movie in the AV room, we can talk quietly to each other.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: So if there's anything that you can't see well, I can tell you what's going on.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Whisperain, come get some rest. Would you like some blueberry raisins?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: I appreciate the offer, but no thanks. After I look at Lara's results, I still have other patients to take care of.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Don't be so focused on taking care of others that you forget to take care of yourself. Your body isn't in great condition either, and needs rest.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Thanks, but you don't have to worry about me so much.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Right, you said you'll bring Lara to a movie. Is it the screening on Saturday?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: *Sigh*... Have you told her about the worst case scenario yet? She might have to enjoy the movie through sound alone by then.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: I... I haven't. She's been really looking forward to it these last few days. I don't want to dampen her spirits.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Yeah, I guess. Whatever the case, letting her do these little things she did before the accident will probably alleviate some stress.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Once her condition stabilizes, I'll bring her some snacks and have a chat with her.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Oh, and I'll bring some for you too, of course. Just be sure to actually have some next time!

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Next time? ...Sure, thank you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Right, so I've asked all the operators I see in the break room to go to the screening this weekend.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: It'll feel more like a movie theater with a bigger crowd, right? It should help the patients rebuild the confidence to interact with others, too.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Right, thank you. I'll always remember my time here at—

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: —Hold on, Dr. Honeyberry. Take a look at this.
Hurry! The movie's about to start!
Who put this together?
Hm... I can't tell, but Honeyberry's the one who suggested I come.
There were no leaflets or notices, and it seems they put a mini-theater together in the AV room in just one night.
No one's checking tickets at the door either. It's all printed by a self-service ticketing machine.
But if we can print tickets, that's gotta mean we can go in and watch, right? It doesn't say anywhere we can't, right?
I've been curious about this movie for a while now. I've wanted to watch it ever since I read Whisperain's review.
Yeah, me too!

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Lara, be careful.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: It's okay, Doctor. It's a little dark, but I can still see the steps with how high they are!

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Huh? This place really feels like a movie theater. There are so many people... Is it really okay for me to go inside?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Don't worry. You've been coming into contact with so many people every day. You won't spread Oripathy to them.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I'll sit in the front row, then.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: It's such a big screen... I can see everything so clearly like this.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Doctor, you don't have to stay with me if you're busy. I'll find my way back to my room.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: No, please. Let me stay and watch the story again.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: —Hold on, Dr. Honeyberry. Take a look at this.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Going by these imaging results, the spread of Originium inside Lara's body is... under control.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Wow, you're right!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Now you two can watch the movie together with no issues!

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Are you still worried about something?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: If there's anything on your mind, you can tell me. It doesn't matter if it's happy or sad, it always feels better if you talk to someone about it.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Don't worry. I'm a certified counselor. It won't be a burden for me.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Besides, how would you know how others will react if you never tell anyone?

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I don't think I understood the movie's ending, but it gave me this kinda weird feeling.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Huh? Doctor, are you crying?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Don't worry about it. It stirs my emotions every time I hear the credits theme.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: There are a lot of different interpretations of the ending. Even I see it differently depending on my mood.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Then I guess I should see it again when I get older.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Thank you for staying with me all this time, Doctor.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Hold on, Lara.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Sorry, but there's something very important that I haven't told you yet.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: As you've noticed, your vision is deteriorating because of your condition.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: It's under control for the time being, but as long as you have Oripathy, Originium will inevitably eat away at your body.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: So you mean... I won't be able to see anything?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Right... I can't say for sure when you'll go blind, but it will happen eventually. All too soon.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Actually, I kind of figured.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: I'm sorry that I've been keeping it from you.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: No worries, Doctor. I've already given it a lot of thought. Actually, I'd even mentally prepared myself for not being able to watch the movie.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: That's why, for the past few days, I've been trying my best to keep my eyes wide open. To remember all the streets, houses, flowers, and grass that I see, how blue the sky is and how white the snow.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I don't know when Oripathy will make my body hurt again... or when I'll wake up one morning and not be able to see.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: But until then, I want to try my best to remember everything that I come across.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: I want to remember everyone that I like too, everyone who takes care of me.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: That way, when I hear their names, I'll remember how they look.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: So even if things do turn out the way I just said, and I slowly forget everything like my old grandpa who doesn't remember who I am...

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Even if there comes a day...

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Even if there comes a day I hear a movie's title but don't remember what it means to me.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Just like the wandering bard who disappears into the rain at the end of the movie. She too once danced in this era's rain.

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Oh, sorry. I finished your sentence again.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: But that's exactly how I feel.

steps.name: Lara
steps.text: Oh, right, about the ending. Do you think the bard went back in the end? Or do you think she stayed with us?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Well, what I think is...

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Oh, that's the girl I always see in the AV room.

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: ...I'm going to borrow the AV room to watch 'Drifting Memories' next Saturday.

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: Want to join me?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: Next Saturday?

steps.name: Whisperain
steps.text: ...I'd love to. Thanks for inviting me.
